key_insight: TALQ uses a large language model to rate 52 symptoms in text, enabling frequent tracking of expressed depressive and anxious states.
clinical_relevance: Text-based symptom tracking could complement infrequent questionnaires, but this study does not establish diagnostic accuracy or clinical benefit.
method: Scored text from 491 members of two online mental health communities every two weeks for one year.
Compared ratings with human annotations and inventories completed by the same model.
Identified 12 replicable symptom factors and examined longitudinal state patterns.
evidence_signal: Ratings were stable across samples and predicted human annotations; sleep disturbance and self-harm content preceded overwhelm and emotional pain, respectively, by two weeks.
watch_item: Findings from online community text may not generalize to clinical populations, and temporal associations do not establish causation.
paper_title: TALQ: A reproducible language model questionnaire for dense measurement of depressive and anxious states
